evidence: The fixed rear three-quarter view, gray muscle-fiber mannequin and mostly stationary seated torso fit the requested presentation. Both hands retain the same machine handles in the inspected frames.

The orange illumination is a narrow vertical stripe directly over the spinal column, extending down the lumbar midline. The paired middle-back muscle bellies remain gray; this does not show the catalog primary middle-back involvement. Confirmed in the full-resolution contracted frame at 3.0 s.
The main pull lowers the handles only to shoulder/head level, with forearms still largely vertical. It does not bring the handles toward the sides of the ribs as specified in motionAnchors.endpoint.

After the main pull and return to overhead reach, the arms dip into another abbreviated pull during the latter part of the second contact sheet, then rise again. The clip therefore includes an extra partial repetition instead of one completed cycle followed by a still finish.
reviews.correctionPrompt: Keep the Anatomical 3D gray fiber mannequin, fixed rear three-quarter camera, seated body and machine. Correct the glow first: show two broad orange muscle regions on either side of the upper-middle back, over the middle trapezius/rhomboid region; keep the spinal bones and narrow central spinal line neutral gray. The orange muscle regions remain visible from the first frame to the last. Use an actual leverage high-row machine whose handles travel from an overhead reach down and back toward the sides of the lower ribs. At the contracted endpoint the elbows are near the torso and drawn behind it, not a hands-at-head lat-pulldown endpoint. Demonstrate exactly one cycle: 0–1s still overhead start;1–3.5s one uninterrupted pull;3.5–4s pause at ribs;4–7s one uninterrupted full overhead return;7–8s absolutely motionless in the original overhead pose. No second elbow bend, pump, bounce or partial repetition after the return. Seat, torso, thigh pads and feet remain fixed; hands never release their handles.
limitations: Inspected two chronological 3 fps contact sheets spanning the 8-second clip, plus full-resolution diagnostic frames. This was sampled-frame inspection, not continuous playback; brief transitions between samples were not evaluated.

evidence: The render has a fixed side view and clear gray muscle-fiber treatment, and both feet remain on the visible footplate. Orange quadriceps highlighting is visible after the opening portion.

The apparatus is a seat carriage on rails aimed toward a footplate braced against the base. The footplate remains fixed while the seat/hip position changes. This contradicts the required stationary reclining seat and separately moving 45-degree footplate sled. The frame 0 and approximately 3.33 s detail frames clearly show the seat-position change and unchanged footplate support.

After the initial knee bend and extension, another lowering phase occurs near the end. The extracted 7.9 s final frame has visibly bent knees; it does not match the nearly straight initial knee position. The requested single complete repetition with a held return is not present.
The quadriceps are entirely gray at frame 0 and in the next sampled opening frame. Their orange coloring fades in later, so the required muscle indication is missing at the start.

The padded backrest and body also change their relative alignment as the knees bend. Together with the fixed footplate, this makes the demonstrated machine mechanics unsuitable for the requested stationary-seat leg press.
reviews.correctionPrompt: Replace the apparatus with a conventional 45-degree sled leg press: a stationary reclining padded seat fixed directly to the floor frame at the lower left, and a separate footplate carriage above/in front of the athlete that visibly slides on two diagonal rails. Only the footplate carriage moves; the seat, pelvis, backrest and torso never translate. Do not put the seat on sliding rails or brace the moving footplate to a fixed floor strut. Keep the pelvis and back against the stationary pad and both heels planted on the moving plate. Use a fixed side camera showing the whole hip-knee-ankle chain and rail travel. The gray anatomical mannequin has orange quadriceps muscle bellies clearly visible from frame 1 through the final frame. Exactly one cycle: 0–1s hold near-straight softly unlocked knees with sled far away;1–3.5s let the sled approach while knees bend to about a right angle;3.5–4s brief bottom pause;4–7s push the sled away while extending to the exact initial knee position;7–8s remain perfectly still at that original position. Do not bend the knees again, rebound, repeat, or finish in the lowered position.
